messages:
alexg: Heads-up — noticed a spike in decode tail latency on the nightly perf job after the FlashAttention variant swap. Small-batch decode (batch=1, seq≈16) 95th went from ~45ms -> ~120ms.
priya_ml: Ugh. Which variant did we flip to? flash_attn_fwd_v2? :thinking_face:
mike_r: We switched the default kernel selector to prefer `flash_attn_fwd_v2` for small seqs last night to optimize prefill throughput. Might be a regression in the decode path where continuous batching interacts with KV cache layout.
alexg: Exactly. I repro locally with continuous batching on. Here's the bench command I used:
```
./bench --mode=decode --model=gpt-open-8k --batch=1 --microbatch=4 --seq=32 --kernel=auto --continuous
```
alexg: nvprof + pprof shows most time in the flash kernel for decode microbatches, but end-to-end there's a lot of kernel relaunch / memcpy overhead.
julia: Can you paste the flame numbers? curious about fused vs paged.
alexg: Quick flame (top few):
```
flash_attn_fwd_v2  62.1%
fused_attention_sm80 25.4%
paged_attention_v1  7.3%
```
alexg: But traces show many 1–2ms gaps between kernels — likely host<->device syncs when KV pages straddle boundaries.
chen_ops: We also have a recent KV page allocator tweak on master that changed page alignment. Could be related.
priya_ml: Do we have test corpus where prefill and decode share the same KV layout? Maybe the continuous-batching prefix reuse is hitting an edge-case.
mike_r: I instrumented the runtime: when decode microbatch < decode_batch_min_tokens (8) the selector falls back to fused_attention for prefill but not for decode. So asymmetry exists.
alexg: That's the key. Prefill path uses one heuristic (favor fused for tiny batches), decode path uses kernel chosen by selector that only sees per-step token count — continuous batching can coalesce steps and make selector pick flash which is poor for microbatches.
julia: Could explain why prefill looked fine in canary but real traffic (with many interleaved streams) regressed.
priya_ml: Repro steps:
1) enable continuous batching
2) run many concurrent single-stream decodes with short prompts
3) toggle kernel selector to prefer fused -> latency back to baseline
mike_r: Temporary mitigation: force decode to use fused when microbatch tokens < 12. Quick flag:
```
service.config.decode_kernel_policy.small_batch_threshold = 12
```
chen_ops: I can roll that as a runtime toggle for canary. But long-term we should fix selector logic.
alexg: Agreed. Hypothesis: flash_attn_v2 has worse kernel launch + workspace allocation overhead for repeated tiny KV cache updates. We should capture per-call allocator stats.
priya_ml: I'll add allocator counters and page-cross event logs. Also will add a microbench that simulates page boundary cases.
julia: Also test paged_attention_v1 in decode-only runs: if it avoids memcpy and keeps pages resident we might prefer it for decode microbatches.
mike_r: Perf experiments to run (assigning):
- @priya_ml: add allocator counters + page event logging + reproduce script
- @alexg: run microbench with `--kernel=paged_attention_v1` and `--kernel=fused_attention_sm80` across seq=[8,16,32]
- @chen_ops: roll flag `small_batch_threshold=12` to canary
- @julia: collect nightly job with continuous batching + new logging
sre-bot: deploy request created: canary rollout of decode small-batch flag to 10% — id: DR-1845
priya_ml: Quick note: pprof samples show the flash kernel has better throughput on large batches but its per-invocation setup cost is ~0.7ms which dominates for 1–4 token microbatches.
alexg: If flash kernel warm path can avoid workspace realloc on repeated calls (reuse per-stream workspace keyed by KV page id) that might close gap.
mike_r: Implementation idea: augment kernel runtime with a `workspace_hint` derived from KV page id; runtime can keep a small LRU of pre-allocated buffers per-stream.
chen_ops: That might increase memory pressure on high-concurrency hosts. Need to simulate worst-case memory usage.
julia: For now let's keep the mitigation flag. We'll triage the allocator reuse plan in the perf sync on Friday.
alexg: Filed perf ticket: PERF-6521 with repro, traces, and initial data. Linking nightly plot: https://perf-redwood/graphs/decode_tail_spike/184501
priya_ml: I'll push a branch with logs this afternoon and ping when ready.
mike_r: Thanks all — good quick triage. Action items above, will check back after canary data.
julia: :thumbsup:
alexg: closing the loop later today with numbers. If anyone hits an easy reproducer, drop in the thread.
